in_english.long_meaning: Corbinian, a name of Christian origin, derived from the Latin words Corvus and Corvinus, meaning Corbinian the near or coming near. It is related to the heart and the prior, one who comes before. In the Christian tradition, Corbinian is associated with the saint who lived in the 8th century and was a monk who founded the Benedictine abbey in Bavaria. The name Corbinian is also associated with the concept of approaching the divine and being prior to the world. It is a name that symbolizes closeness to God and a desire to come near to Him.
